title: Celebrity Club records: Nat Pierce, Black and Blue, Batan, Swinging Like Tate
summary: Tate lists his recordings including a 1954 album with Inez Washington and Swinging Like Tate with Stanley Dance.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: What were the best records that came out of the Celebrity Club? The only one I know is the M.P.S.
Actually, I don't know if that was the best one, though. Let me see. That's the one with Nat Pierce.
Yeah, Nat's on that. Well, we did one for Monesta (Phonetic) We did two for Black and Blue.

Un-huh. And I'll try to get one to you. It's -- I'll try to get you one. And we did one in '54, we made an album for -- what the hell was the name of that -- I'm trying to remember the name of the -- Batan, it was a Batan label, B-a-t-a-n, but he sold it and I've heard them things on like now two different labels and that's why it's so confusing to me, you know? But it was originally Batan label by a Jewish fella by the name of Saul Rabinowitz He was the President of that company. And they were very -- that was a very good album. We used a girl singer by the name of Inez Washington. She could sing her can off! Ballads, blues, anything, and she only made -- I think she made a record with Cab afterwards, but that was the only two records she made. She went to South America with Cab and I think he recorded her. She was a hell of a singer. She died several years ago. I'll try to get you -- I think I got some. I want you to hear it, man.
Then we made some -- Stanley Dance came over. Oh,
yeah, I think that's the best. That was the best one, on Felstead

"Swinging Like Tate." I think that would be about the best one. On the other side, I had some of the Basie-ites and you know, like Earl and Dickey and Bub and I think I had Jo Jones. Jo didn't play too good that day, though. And let me see, what else?
